title: Isolated-site Connectivity Matrix and Upgrade Rollback SLAs for Private Deployments
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define a deterministic connectivity matrix, preflight checks, and concrete rollback SLAs for Private/VPC (isolated-site) deployments. This ticket captures requirements, acceptance criteria, and an operational playbook for upgrades and emergency rollbacks in egress-restricted environments.
background: Customers operating in regulated or air-restricted environments have asked for clearer guarantees around upgrades and the network interactions required during a maintenance window. Current documentation is fragmented and engineering teams have reported ambiguous failure modes during offline upgrades. We need a single source of truth that product, SRE, and Solutions Engineering can rely on.
goals: Produce a documented connectivity matrix mapping each control-plane and data-plane interaction required for install, upgrade, and rollback
Specify preflight checks that can run in fully isolated clusters (no external egress) and determine pass/fail criteria
Define rollback SLAs and automated snapshot points to ensure recoverability if an upgrade violates health criteria
Ensure compatibility notes for KMS/HSM-backed key rotation during upgrades
Provide a validation plan for Solutions Engineering to test with customer replicas
non_goals: Designing a new offline package distribution mechanism (this ticket assumes existing offline media workflows)
Full implementation of automated in-place DB migrations (scope limited to validation and fallback)
requirements: Connectivity Matrix: CSV-style listing of endpoints, protocols, ports, direction (in/out), and purpose (e.g., license check, telemetry write, image fetch). Must cover: control plane, runtime nodes, registry access, KMS, metrics/alerting endpoints.

Preflight Suite: A scriptable set of checks that can be run from the customer's bastion host. Must include: DNS resolution checks, port reachability to listed endpoints, PKI validation for certificate chains, and dry-run of schema migrations where applicable.

Offline Upgrade Path: Definition of steps for applying an upgrade via customer-provided media, including integrity verification (signed images), node draining semantics, KV cache warming expectations, and post-upgrade smoke checks.

Rollback SLAs: Time-to-safe-state objectives and an ordered list of rollback actions (automated snapshot restore -> service restart -> manual intervention). Each action must include expected duration and success criteria.
Health Gates: Explicit health metrics and thresholds used to abort an upgrade (e.g., API p95 increase > 2x sustained for 5 minutes, failed Liveness checks > 3 nodes).
Observability Hooks: Required tracing and logs to capture pre/post-upgrade diffs; minimal retention window for these artifacts must be stated to aid postmortems.
KMS/HSM Notes: Steps for rotating or re-binding keys during an upgrade without losing access to persisted secrets; fallbacks if external KMS is unreachable during maintenance window.
Roles and Approvals: Which personas must approve a rollout and which can execute an emergency rollback. Tie to Console RBAC roles.
Runbook: A concise playbook (max 2 pages) that SRE/SE can execute; includes decision points, commands, and contact escalation matrix.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable connectivity matrix (CSV) is checked into the repo and referenced in Private Deployment docs
Preflight Suite executes in an isolated environment using only customer-provided hosts and returns deterministic pass/fail codes
A documented offline upgrade procedure validated by Solutions Engineering on two distinct customer-like topologies (single-AZ small cluster and multi-AZ medium cluster), with signed test artifacts
Rollback procedure validated in a staged test where simulated failure triggers automated snapshot restore and meets the stated SLA <= 20 minutes to safe-state for small clusters
All health gates and metrics used by the upgrade controller are listed with thresholds and unit tests that simulate threshold breaches
KMS/HSM key rebind steps verified in a dry-run with a mock KMS and documented fallback if the KMS is unreachable
Runbook reviewed and approved by SRE lead and Solutions Engineering; signoff captured in comments and doc link
Security review completed and any action items tracked as child tickets
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Author connectivity matrix and preflight automation (dev); Phase 2: Run validations in staging and with two SE testbeds; Phase 3: Publish docs and runbook, ship as part of private-2025.1. Communication: announce to customers with private deployments and offer two-week window for adoption support.
test_plan: Test A: Preflight-only test in isolated VPC with simulated blocked egress -> expect clear failure mode and remediation hints
Test B: Offline upgrade via signed media on single-AZ cluster -> validate service smoke checks and ability to rollback within SLA
Test C: KMS failure during upgrade simulated -> verify fallback path does not decrypt secrets and aborts upgrade safely
Test D: Load test post-upgrade to verify latency/regression thresholds are within acceptable bounds
migration_notes: Customers using older private packages may require manual image signature verification steps; add a migration helper script
Provide a checklist for customers to snapshot DB state before scheduling the maintenance window
Recommend 30-60 minute maintenance windows for medium clusters to allow for validation and possible rollback
open_questions: Should the connectivity matrix be enforced by an optional admission controller during installs? (Eng input required)
What is the canonical storage location and retention policy for upgrade artifacts collected during a private upgrade?
Do we require a bundled minimal telemetry sink (local file + customer-upload) to aid postmortems when external telemetry is disallowed?
decisions: Use CSV for the connectivity matrix to maximize copy/paste and scripting friendliness
Preflight suite will return non-zero exit codes for failed checks and produce a human-readable remediation section
Rollback SLA for small clusters set to 20 minutes to safe-state; medium clusters set to 60 minutes (documented as target, not a hard SLA)
